sources.reviewer_note: Frankfurt provisioned-mode and enhanced-fan-out meters; long-term retention beyond seven days is outside v1.
Capacity proof uses provisioned shards and account-quota preflight.
Raw device ingress uses 5-KB message chunks; rules and actions are independent meters.
Large raw telemetry peak and payload remain below documented defaults.
Command execution is charged separately from IoT Core messaging.
First x86 duration tier is sufficient for the bounded scenarios.
Standard workflow chosen for durable auditable execution.
Rejected telemetry alternative remains price-visible but is not scenario-ranked.
Control and outcome channels use FIFO topics and SQS subscriptions.
One send, receive, and delete request is modeled per delivered control message.
Full-record Kinesis terminal failures use S3 Standard as the dead-letter owner.
Standard custom-log ingestion; the global five-GB log free tier is applied once.
Existing reviewed transfer-catalog tiers are reused without emergency fallback.
Destination trust must constrain issuer, audience, and workload subject or issuance assignment.
Standard includes up to seven-day retention; ingress is rounded in 64-KB units.
Large is sharded across 15 namespaces because throughput units are namespace-scoped.
Rejected telemetry alternative remains price-visible but is not scenario-ranked.
Hourly base meter is used; the alternative monthly base meter is not double-counted.
Retail API quantities are normalized from units of ten executions; selected instances use 2 GiB.
On-demand Flex executions are billed for at least one second and then in 100-ms increments.
The shared workflow contains three built-in actions and one standard connector notification call.
Scenario allocation is S1 x1, S2 x3, and S3 x1.
Cloud-to-device queues are selected instead of non-durable direct methods.
Pay-as-you-go Analytics Logs; the requested 30-day retention is included.
Existing reviewed Europe internet-egress tiers are reused.
Federated identity credential constrains issuer, subject, and audience.
Throughput includes publishing and every subscriber delivery; topic retention is shared by subscriptions.
Large uses six subscription worker pools with 21 streams each; push is rejected for Large delivery.

sources.service_family: Google Cloud Run services and worker pools
sources.reviewer_note: Request-based adapters use the documented 0.167-vCPU/256-MiB function shape; worker pools use 1 vCPU/512 MiB and are billed for their full lifetime after the shared free tier.
Three internal and one external step are billed in separate 1,000-step increments.
Regional Standard-cluster management fee; the zonal free-tier credit is intentionally not applied.
On-demand e2-standard-8 node price in europe-west1; three nodes are a scenario allocation, not a provider price fact.
Balanced Persistent Disk capacity price; 100 GiB per node is a scenario allocation, not a provider price fact.
One external passthrough network load-balancer forwarding rule is modeled for the command boundary.
The fixed 30-day retention is included in log-bucket ingestion.
Existing reviewed premium-tier Europe internet-egress schedule is reused.
GCP has no managed MQTT replacement; the hosted broker must remain explicit.
The previously selected 5.8.8 image is EOL at the research cut-off and is rejected.
A clustered supported EMQX deployment cannot produce a reproducible public software-price input.
Apache-2.0 avoids software-license cost, but ASF incubation remains an explicit PoC-only operational-maturity risk; Pub/Sub stays the durable command owner.
Provider and service-account bindings must constrain mapped workload attributes.
